_meta.description: Discount rate, inflation, fuel escalation, electricity escalation, and payback assumptions.
_meta.critical_caveat: The discount-rate/cost-of-capital layer is now traceable to an actual dated RBI policy rate (Step 11) rather than an assumed figure -- this should anchor the whole file.

discount_rate.base_rate_source: RBI repo rate, held unchanged at the 3-5 August 2026 MPC meeting (6-0 unanimous); last moved by a cut from 5.5% to 5.25% in December 2025.
discount_rate.transmission_mechanism: Since October 2019, all floating-rate bank loans to micro and small enterprises must be linked to this External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR), not an internal bank rate -- so the repo rate is a direct input, not an approximation.

msme_lending_rates.point_estimate_note: Midpoint of the bank-reported range -- recommended over an unverified 7-12% claim seen on some aggregator sites.

rate_source_conflict.resolution: Treat 9-16% (EBLR + spread) as the working default for unsubsidized MSME term loans. Rates quoted below ~9% almost certainly reflect a specific concessional scheme (SIDBI Green Finance, KVIC ISEC, etc.) and should be tagged with that scheme's name, not used as a general market rate.

financing_access_context.note: Justifies modeling a distinct 'MSME accessible financing' scenario vs a 'theoretical optimal financing' scenario -- actual capital access is a real constraint layer separate from technology economics.

list: Traditional finance channels insufficient in scale
Green premium -- clean technology costs more upfront than incumbent fossil alternatives
Cost of capital disproportionately high for MSMEs specifically
No domestic carbon market in India (removes a potential revenue/incentive channel)
Lack of investor confidence in the space
decarbonization_financing_barriers_wef.macro_context: IEA estimates India needs USD 160 billion/year in investment across its energy economy through 2030 to hit net-zero goals -- roughly 3x current investment levels (not MSME-specific, but useful top-line framing).

niti_aayog_financing_proposals.status: proposed, sector-wide fund, not yet allocated/disbursed -- do not treat as a per-project subsidy amount

aggregate_msme_cluster_retrofit.source: 7-cluster CSTEP-aligned study, cited via Drishti IAS -- usable as a sanity-check default if technology-specific payback data is unavailable
aggregate_msme_cluster_retrofit.attribution_caveat: Could not fully confirm whether this is the CSTEP study directly or a related study referenced in the same reporting wave -- verify against primary TERI/CSTEP source documents before final citation.

waste_heat_recovery_bee_pali_case.source: BEE-run DPR for a textile cluster (Pali, Rajasthan) stenter WHR installation

solar_pv_vendor_claimed.caveat: Vendor-claimed -- treat as optimistic upper bound, not typical.

electricity_tariff_escalation.signal_source: Karnataka KERC multi-year filings show a confirmed rising trajectory: +0.67 INR/kWh (FY25-26), +0.75 (FY26-27), +0.91 (FY27-28), plus fixed-charge hikes stacked on top.
electricity_tariff_escalation.note: Use as an escalation-RATE signal (rising trend confirmed), not as a precise national point estimate -- only one state's trajectory is documented in detail.

coal.evidence: Coal India (CIL) notified non-coking coal price revisions are step-changes, not a smooth annual curve -- e.g. an ~10% board-approved hike effective 9 Jan 2018. Ministry of Coal representative-price series (via CEIC) shows individual grades moving sharply within single months in 2026 (e.g. Grade G13 rose from INR 1,716/t in May 2026 to INR 1,849/t in June 2026, ~7.8% in one month), confirming volatility rather than a stable trend.
coal.confidence: Low-Medium -- no official CIL or Ministry of Coal multi-year escalation *rate* is published; the 5-7%/yr figure is an analyst-style planning assumption derived from the historical pattern of periodic step hikes, not a quoted government projection.
coal.source: Ministry of Coal representative price data (via CEIC); Coal India price-revision press coverage (Business Standard, Jan 2018).

natural_gas.evidence: Domestic (APM) gas price is formula-based and its escalation is directly documented: post the 2023 Kirit Parikh Committee reform, the APM ceiling was held at USD 6.5/mmBtu for FY24 and FY25, then legislated to rise by USD 0.25/mmBtu per year -- taking the ceiling to USD 6.75/mmBtu (Apr 2025) and USD 7.00/mmBtu (Apr 2026). On a ~USD 6.75-7.00 base this is roughly a 3.5-4% annual step. The floor is fixed at USD 4/mmBtu.
natural_gas.confidence: High for the regulated/APM segment (~60-70% of domestic gas supply) -- this is a codified government formula, not an estimate. Market-priced gas (deepwater/HPHT fields, e.g. KG-D6) and imported LNG move with global benchmarks and are materially more volatile; the 3.5-4%/yr figure applies to APM-priced gas only.
natural_gas.source: Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC), Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas -- monthly domestic natural gas price notifications; Kirit Parikh Committee gas-pricing reform (2023).

biomass.evidence: No official multi-year biomass price escalation series exists, but a rising-demand trend is documented: the Ministry of Power's mandatory coal co-firing policy required a minimum 5% biomass-pellet blend from FY2024-25, rising to 7% from FY2025-26 (25-year policy horizon), creating structural demand growth against a large but logistically constrained ~230 million tonne/year surplus. Market pellet prices reported in early 2026 (~INR 7,500-10,500/tonne) sit above earlier-reported ranges (~INR 6,500-9,500/tonne), consistent with upward pressure, though these are not a controlled like-for-like series.
biomass.confidence: Low -- this is a directional/qualitative trend (rising blend mandate + limited pellet-processing capacity vs. raw-residue surplus), not a quoted escalation rate. The 4-6%/yr figure is a working planning assumption, not a cited government or CSTEP/TERI projection.
biomass.source: Ministry of Power biomass co-firing policy and benchmark pellet price notification (Nov 2023, revised policy effective FY2024-25); market pellet-price reporting (PelletRates, early 2026) -- cross-check against TERI/CEEW biomass economics reports before final citation.

fuel_price_escalation.overall_note: Coal and biomass escalation figures are working planning assumptions inferred from documented step-changes and demand trends, not quoted official escalation rates -- flag as such (Medium/Low confidence) in the evidence register. Natural gas (APM segment) is the one fuel with a directly codified, high-confidence annual escalation formula.

general_inflation.cpi_target_source: RBI Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework, retained at 4% +/-2% for the 5-year period 1 April 2026 - 31 March 2031, under Section 45-ZA of the RBI Act, 1934.
general_inflation.near_term_cpi_projection_source: RBI August 2026 MPC statement: headline CPI inflation for FY2026-27 projected at 5.0% (Q2 ~4.7%, Q3 ~5.9%, Q4 ~5.5%), after headline CPI rose to 4.4% in June 2026 -- above the 4% target after 16 consecutive months below it.
general_inflation.recommended_default_rationale: Use the RBI's own FY2026-27 headline CPI projection (5.0%) as the working escalation/inflation input for near-term (1-3 year) cash-flow modeling, since it is the most current, officially sourced figure. For longer-horizon (10-25 year) project lifetimes, the mid-point of the RBI's statutory long-run target band (4%) is the more defensible anchor, since MPC point projections are only issued 1-2 years out.
general_inflation.confidence: High -- both figures are directly sourced from RBI's own statutory target and its most recent (Aug 2026) MPC statement, not third-party estimates.

gaps_and_flags: General inflation is now sourced (RBI FIT target 4% +/-2% for 2026-2031; RBI's own FY2026-27 CPI projection of 5.0%) -- no longer a gap. Recommend 5.0% for near-term modeling, 4.0% for long-run/terminal-value modeling.

Fuel price escalation is now populated for all three fuels, but confidence differs sharply: natural gas (APM segment) has a High-confidence, formula-based ~3.5-4%/yr rate; coal (~5-7%/yr) and biomass (~4-6%/yr) are Low/Medium-confidence planning assumptions inferred from historical step-changes and demand-mandate trends, not quoted official escalation series -- do not present these three with equal confidence in the deliverable.
The aggregate 2.4-year payback benchmark has an unresolved attribution question (CSTEP vs. a related study) -- verify against primary TERI/CSTEP source documents before final citation.

RBI data confirms the financing-COST and general-inflation layers well; it does not and cannot provide MSME energy-consumption or sector data -- that remains sourced from BEE/World Bank/NITI Aayog/CEEW.

Coal and biomass escalation rates should be re-verified against a primary CIL/Ministry of Coal multi-year price series and a TERI/CEEW biomass economics report respectively before being cited as anything more than working assumptions in a judged deliverable.
